question.text: Mr. Rajesh Nair, a resident individual LP of Lotus Venture Fund (Cat I AIF), receives pass-through LTCG of INR 40 lakh (gross) on sale of unlisted equity shares held by the fund for 40 months. His slab otherwise is 30%. What is Rajesh's incremental tax on this LTCG under Section 112 (post Finance (No.2) Act 2024, basic rate, ignore surcharge/cess)?

answer.text: Exempt up to INR 1.25 lakh, balance at 10%

explanation.text: The Logic: Post Finance (No.2) Act 2024 (w.e.f. 23-07-2024), LTCG on unlisted equity is taxed at a uniform 12.5% WITHOUT indexation benefit. Holding >24 months for unlisted qualifies as long-term. 12.5% x INR 40 lakh = INR 5 lakh. The INR 1.25 lakh exemption (option D) is ONLY for STT-paid listed equity/equity-oriented MF/ business trust units under Section 112A — not unlisted. The Trap: Option A is the pre-23-07-2024 regime (20% with indexation). Option C uses slab — wrong for LTCG. Option D wrongly applies the 112A threshold to unlisted. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests the 'what rate?' level; XIX-C expects the manager to issue Form 64C pre-populated with head-wise LTCG so the LP's CA computes correctly. Manager's Pro-Tip: Time exits cleverly: the 23-07-2024 cutover killed indexation. For high-cost-base private-market positions acquired long ago, run the pre/post comparison — some sponsors pushed exits before 23-07-2024 to grandfather indexation.
